title: range===0 branch renders every boundary as an identical overlapping line at x=50% (no dedup, no off-range filter)
description: In the all-values-equal branch, boundaries.map renders one <line> per boundary but hard-codes x1/x2 to "50%" for all of them, so N boundaries produce N identical lines stacked exactly on top of each other — visually indistinguishable from a single line, and the extra DOM nodes are pure waste. It also omits the off-range filtering the main branch applies (lines 90-91 `if (xPct < 0 || xPct > 100) return null`), so boundaries that don't actually fall on the single value still draw a centre line, which is arguably misleading. At most one centre marker is meaningful here.
evidence: Lines 38-52: `boundaries.map((_b, i) => { ... <line key={i} x1="50%" ... x2="50%" ... /> })` — `_b` (the boundary value) is unused, so all lines are positionally identical regardless of value; compare the main branch which positions each line by value and filters out-of-range ones (lines 89-91).
est_reduction: ~8 lines / collapse N identical lines to a single conditional marker
behavior_preservation: Rendering one centre line (or none when no boundary equals the value) instead of N overlapping identical lines is visually equivalent; the only observable change is the count of <line> nodes, which BandingHistogram.test.tsx asserts only for range>0 cases (the single/same-value tests check svg presence and, for negatives, range>0).
